arxiv-2105-01136.title: Learning Good State and Action Representations for Markov Decision Process via Tensor Decomposition
arxiv-2105-01136.creator: Chengzhuo Ni chengzhuo.ni@princeton.eduDepartment of Electrical & Computer EngineeringPrinceton UniversityYaqi Duan yaqid@mit.eduLaboratory for Information & Decision SystemsMassachusetts Institute of TechnologyMunther Dahleh dahleh@mit.eduElectrical Engineering & Computer Science DepartmentMassachu
arxiv-2105-01136.description: Abstract The transition kernel of a continuous-state-action Markov decision process (MDP) admits a natural tensor structure. This paper proposes a tensor-inspired unsupervised learning method to identify meaningful low-dimensional state and action representations from empirical trajectories. The method exploits the MDP’s tensor structure by kernelization, importance sampling and low-Tucker-rank approximation.

arxiv-2206-07642.title: Convergence and Price of Anarchy Guarantees of the Softmax Policy Gradient in Markov Potential Games
arxiv-2206-07642.creator: Dingyang Chen, Qi Zhang, Thinh T. Doan
arxiv-2206-07642.description: Abstract We study the performance of policy gradient methods for the subclass of Markov games known as Markov potential games (MPGs), which extends the notion of normal-form potential games to the stateful setting and includes the important special case of the fully cooperative setting where the agents share an identical reward function.

arxiv-2304-05841.title: Exploring Diffusion Models for Unsupervised Video Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2304-05841.creator: Anil Osman Tur, Nicola Dall’Asen, Cigdem Beyan, Elisa Ricci
arxiv-2304-05841.description: Abstract This paper investigates the performance of diffusion models for video anomaly detection (VAD) within the most challenging but also the most operational scenario in which the data annotations are not used. As being sparse, diverse, contextual, and often ambiguous, detecting abnormal events precisely is a very ambitious task.

arxiv-2305-07532.title: Measurements of inclusive and differential cross sections for the Higgs boson production and decay to four-leptons in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2305-07532.description: Abstract Measurements of the inclusive and differential fiducial cross sections for the Higgs boson production in the \PH → \PZ ​ \PZ → 4 ​ ℓ \PH\to\PZ\PZ\to 4\ell ( ℓ = \Pe , \Pgm \ell=\Pe,\Pgm ) decay channel are presented.

arxiv-2309-07886.title: Vortex Lattices in Active Nematics with Periodic Obstacle Arrays
arxiv-2309-07886.creator: Cody D. Schimming, C. J. O. Reichhardt, C. Reichhardt
arxiv-2309-07886.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cody D. Schimming, C. J. O. Reichhardt, C. Reichhardt. We numerically model a two-dimensional active nematic confined by a periodic array of fixed obstacles. Even in the passive nematic, the appearance of topological defects is unavoidable due to planar anchoring by the obstacle surfaces. We show that a vortex lattice state emerges as activity is increased, and that this lattice may be tuned from “ferromagnetic” to “antiferromagnetic” by varying the gap size between obstacles.

arxiv-2310-02551.title: Apex Graphs and Cographs
arxiv-2310-02551.creator: Jagdeep Singh, Vaidy Sivaraman, Thomas Zaslavsky
arxiv-2310-02551.description: Abstract . A class 𝒢 \mathcal{G} of graphs is called hereditary if it is closed under taking induced subgraphs. We denote by 𝒢 apex \mathcal{G}^{\mathrm{apex}} the class of graphs G G that contain a vertex v v such that G − v G-v is in 𝒢 \mathcal{G} .

arxiv-2404-13823.title: Thouless pumping and trapping of two-component gap solitons
arxiv-2404-13823.creator: Hao Lyu, Yongping Zhang, Thomas Busch
arxiv-2404-13823.description: Abstract We study Thouless pumping and arresting of gap solitons in a two-component Bose gas loaded into an optical superlattice. We show that, depending on the atomic interactions and chemical potentials, the two solitons can be simultaneously pumped or trapped, but we also identify regimes where one soliton is pumped and the other arrested.

arxiv-2406-15940.title: Beyond Individual Facts: Investigating Categorical Knowledge Locality of Taxonomy and Meronomy Concepts in GPT Models
arxiv-2406-15940.creator: Christopher Burger, Yifan Hu, Thai le
arxiv-2406-15940.description: Abstract The location of knowledge within Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT)-like models has seen extensive recent investigation. However, much of the work is focused towards determining locations of individual facts, with the end goal being the editing of facts that are outdated, erroneous, or otherwise harmful, without the time and expense of retraining the entire model.

arxiv-2502-05153.title: Hummingbird: High Fidelity Image Generation via Multimodal Context Alignment
arxiv-2502-05153.creator: Minh-Quan Le, Gaurav Mittal, Tianjian Meng, A S M Iftekhar, Vishwas Suryanarayanan, Barun Patra, Dimitris Samaras, Mei Chen
arxiv-2502-05153.description: Abstract While diffusion models are powerful in generating high-quality, diverse synthetic data for object-centric tasks, existing methods struggle with scene-aware tasks such as Visual Question Answering (VQA) and Human-Object Interaction (HOI) Reasoning, where it is critical to preserve scene attributes in generated images consistent with a multimodal context, i.e. a reference image with accompanying text guidance query.

arxiv-2509-05613.title: Collective effects in O-O and Ne-Ne collisions at s NN \sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36 TeV 5.36\text{\,}\mathrm{TeV} from a hybrid approach
arxiv-2509-05613.creator: Lucas Constantin 1,2 , Niklas Götz 1,2 , Carl B. Rosenkvist 1,2,3 and Hannah Elfner 3,1,2,4
arxiv-2509-05613.description: Abstract Many features of heavy-ion collisions are well described by hybrid approaches, where the droplet of strongly coupled quark gluon plasma (QGP) is modeled by hydrodynamics and the subsequent dilute stage is performed with a hadronic transport model. Conventionally, the formation of a QGP is well established in larger collision systems like Lead and Gold.

arxiv-2510-10846.title: DUAL-Bench: Measuring Over-Refusal and Robustness in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2510-10846.creator: Kaixuan Ren, Preslav Nakov, Usman Naseem
arxiv-2510-10846.description: Abstract As vision–language models (VLMs) become increasingly capable, maintaining a balance between safety and usefulness remains a central challenge. Safety mechanisms, while essential, can backfire, causing over-refusal, where models decline benign requests out of excessive caution. Yet, no existing benchmark has systematically addressed over-refusal in the visual modality.

arxiv-2510-19452.title: The vertex visibility number of graphs
arxiv-2510-19452.creator: Dhanya Roy, Gabriele Di Stefano, Sandi Klavžar, Aparna Lakshmanan S
arxiv-2510-19452.description: Abstract If x ∈ V ⁡ ( G ) x\in V(G) , then S ⊆ V ⁡ ( G ) ∖ { x } S\subseteq V(G)\setminus\{x\} is an x x -visibility set if for any y ∈ S y\in S there exists a shortest x , y x,y -path avoiding S S .

pmc-11390509.title: Ferulic acid suppresses the inflammation and apoptosis in Kawasaki disease through activating the AMPK/mTOR/NF-κB pathway
pmc-11390509.creator: Huilan Wu, Yijia Wang, Pingping Tan, Yuqing Ran, Yuting Guan, Songwei Qian, Xing Feng, Yalan Jiang, Yongmiao Peng, Ke Sheng, Haitao Xi, Weiping Ji, Xiaoling Guo
pmc-11390509.description: BackgroundKawasaki disease (KD) is a self-limiting and acute systemic vasculitis of unknown etiology, mainly affecting children. Ferulic acid (FA), a natural phenolic substance, has multiple pharmacological properties, including anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptosis, and anti-fibrosis, and so on. So far, the protective effects of FA on KD have not been explored.

pmc-11546801.title: From Plaques to Pathways in Alzheimer’s Disease: The Mitochondrial-Neurovascular-Metabolic Hypothesis
pmc-11546801.creator: Sarah Kazemeini, Ahmed Nadeem-Tariq, Ryan Shih, John Rafanan, Nabih Ghani, Thomas A. Vida
pmc-11546801.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) presents a public health challenge due to its progressive neurodegeneration, cognitive decline, and memory loss. The amyloid cascade hypothesis, which postulates that the accumulation of amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptides initiates a cascade leading to AD, has dominated research and therapeutic strategies. The failure of recent Aβ-targeted therapies to yield conclusive benefits necessitates further exploration of AD pathology.

pmc-12715202.title: Development and application of formation damage mitigation system for heavy oil reservoir
pmc-12715202.creator: Xi Lu, Lin Meng, Haibo Wang, Changbo Zhai, Tong Zhou, Wenfang Song, Jianfang Sun
pmc-12715202.description: A compound chemical system was developed to address the formation damage in heavy oil reservoirs caused by asphaltene deposition and clay swelling. The dynamic process of asphaltene deposition was simulated through laboratory experiments and the effect of clay types and their mass fractions were investigated.
